info.title: BioID API
info.description:
Identify the biomolecules in a molecular dynamics simulation: upload the
files, poll the run, read the identifications.

* **REST API guide**: [/documentation/rest-api/](/documentation/rest-api/)
* **results.json structure**: [/documentation/results-json/](/documentation/results-json/)
* **For AI assistants**: the MCP server at `/mcp` ([guide](/documentation/mcp/))

Typical flow: `POST /api/v1/runs` (multipart: `files`, optional `run_name`,
`preset`, `config_json`) → poll `GET /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/status` until
`pipeline.status` is `success` or `failed` → `GET .../molecules`,
`.../verification`, `.../download/results.csv` or `.../download/results.json`.
No account is needed. Each file may be up to 128 MiB.

post.description:
Create a new run by uploading input files and optionally a config file.

``preset`` (see GET /runs/config/options) is applied first, then
``config_file`` or ``config_json``; only per-run tunable fields may change.

``queue``: "web" (default) or "repository" (campaigns: own workers and
automatic retries; needs the X-Queue-Token header, issued on the admin page).

The pipeline runs in the background via Celery. Returns immediately with run status.

post.description: Upload simulation files as multipart `files` (repeat the field for several files; GROMACS, AMBER, CHARMM/NAMD, LAMMPS, PDB/mmCIF or a zip/tar bundle; 128 MiB per file). Optional form fields: `run_name`, `preset` (`balanced`, `quick`, `exact`, `deep`; see `GET /api/v1/runs/config/options`) and `config_json` (only the fields that differ from the defaults, e.g. `{"verification": {"verify_top_n": 50}}`). Returns the `run_id`; the run is queued and processed in the background. 422 if a file name or the configuration is not accepted.

post.description:
Re-run all existing runs by copying their input files and config into new run directories.

For each existing run:
- Copies input files from old run to new run directory
- Copies config.ini if it exists, otherwise uses default config
- Creates a new results.json with queued status
- Enqueues a new Celery pipeline task

Old runs are not modified or deleted.

Returns:
    RerunAllResponse with list of new runs, skipped runs, and count

Operators only: needs X-Admin-Token equal to BAT3_ADMIN_TOKEN (404 when
that is unset, as on the public service).
Starts a new run with the same input files and configuration; returns the new `run_id`.

post.description:
Start queue processing via the CANONICAL dispatcher (F-26 reroute, 2026-10-06).

Previously dispatched legacy schedule_validation directly (20 rows, NO
Bat3Run bookkeeping, NULL queue linkage, and an UNSERVED SPLIT-BRAIN
layout /data/validation/entries/<id> + /data/validation/results/<id>/ -
the path that produced the only 3 unlinked queue rows in the campaign).
Now delegates to queue_processor.process_validation_queue: real Bat3Run
(validation-<eid>-<14ts>, servable), exact FK linkage, retry budget.
External contract preserved: {"success", "message", "dispatched"}.
Perform bulk action on queue items (pause, resume, clear, retry, queue_all_pending).
Pause queue processing.
Resume queue processing.
Stop queue processing (cancel all queued items).
Clear all queued items.
Restart a specific worker (placeholder - would need K8s integration).

Per-segment selector into the system mmCIF (BACKEND_GAPS G9, additive).

Persisted at export under ``render/segment_selectors``.

the segment's rows in the exported file's atom_site loop (0-based;

virtual minority segments whose atoms share the parent
``auth_asym_id`` chain (``chains``).

RunStageProgress.title: RunStageProgress
RunStageProgress.description:
Per-molecule identification progress (v3.143, BACKEND_GAPS G2).

Computed read-side from persisted state: a segment is "searched"
once its identifiers block exists, "searching" while the
identify_molecules stage is running for a segment that already has
signatures, and "waiting" otherwise. Only segments the pipeline
decided to identify (fragments/segments ∪ signature-bearing universe
segments) participate — checking-only and signature-less molecules
are excluded and keep the UI's own not_searched rendering.
